newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air control unions call strike at Paris Orly.
newsitem.headline: Air control unions call strike at Paris Orly.

text.p: French air traffic control unions said on Monday they were calling a one-day strike for April 30 at Paris Orly airport, asking for equal pay and conditions with controllers at the Roissy-Charles de Gaulle airport.
The CFDT and USAC/CGT unions said they were protesting against the exclusion of Orly staff from moves towards creating a Paris region air control organisation.
Wednesday, April 30 marks the eve of a long weekend holiday in France starting on May Day holiday when many people take the Friday off.

On Sunday, lingering pilots' strikes disrupted flights in France. Air France Europe cancelled about 40 percent of its flights after some pilots' unions voted to extend a two-day stoppage that began on Friday until Monday evening.
The pilots of the mainly domestic airline have staged a string of stoppages to protest at pay cuts and what they say are unacceptable working conditions in a merger with parent Air France.
About a third of Sunday's flights were grounded at TAT and Air Liberte, the French subsidiaries of British Airways, due to a strike by cabin crew, officials said.

Pilots at the TAT and Air Liberte resumed work at midday on Sunday after a 17-day strike, saying they had won some concessions on pay and conditions. But the flight attendants extended their stoppage, saying their demands had not been met.
